structured_output.what_is_happening: JIRACHI "Last pack magic" is one of at least 10 copycat tokens all named after the same trending Pokémon story, a Dexerto post about pulling a Jirachi card from a last pack. This one launched on a Meteora virtual curve (stonkfun) and migrated right away. It rose about 300% in its first hour, then fell about 63% in the 5 minutes before detection. Its h1 turnover is about 20x liquidity, and the flow looks bot-driven: 1,404 unique buyers in the last hour against only 89 unique sellers, with 63 wallets tagged as bundlers. One unlabeled wallet holds 80% of supply. The creator has launched 38 tokens and has already closed out of this one.

narrative.description: A viral Pokémon TCG moment (Dexerto post about pulling Jirachi from a last pack). It's a light, meme-able news hook, but it leads to one tweet rather than a lasting story.
narrative.why_spreading: A Dexerto news post was picked up by many launchers at once. At least 10 tokens with the same name appeared within about 80 minutes, which points to a race among launchers to capture the ticker rather than genuine community interest.

token_connection.why_this_token: The name matches the story, but it is one of many copies. It was not the first launched, it is not the most liquid, and it does not have the most volume.
token_connection.competing_tokens: HMD6... was created about 18 minutes earlier and is larger ($469k mcap, $870k h1 volume). HUji... has $1.26M h1 volume. DgteW... has $852k h1 volume. Two tokens at about $1.4M mcap show liquidity roughly equal to mcap, which looks faked. There is also a pump.fun copy.

authenticity.evidence: GMGN tags 63 wallets as bundlers. The buyer/seller split is extremely lopsided: 2,096 unique buyers against 93 unique sellers over h6, which points to many small bot buys while a handful of wallets sell. One unlabeled holder has 80% of supply. The creator has 38 prior launches and has already exited (creator_close). The price then dropped 63% in 5 minutes.
authenticity.uncertainty: The 80% holder could be a Meteora curve or pool vault that RugCheck failed to label. If so, the real concentration of supply is lower.

structural_risks: One unlabeled wallet holds 80% of supply, and GeckoTerminal puts the top 10 at 96%
RugCheck flags one market as having 0% of its LP locked
Price just fell 63% in 5 minutes, which fits distribution into the pump
A serial deployer (38 tokens) who has already closed out
About 10 same-name competitors are splitting the flow

structured_output.counterargument: Buying is still heavy: 275 buys against 239 sells in the last 5 minutes, and 1,400 unique buyers in the last hour. The token already reached about $760k at its ATH price, so a 63% flush could leave room for a rebound. A 2x from the post-dump price only means getting back to around the earlier ATH area, and meme races sometimes let one copy rebound hard when the story keeps trending. The 80% holder may just be a curve vault, and GMGN reports an LP burn ratio of 1.0.
unknowns: What the 80% top-holder wallet is (a pool vault or an insider)

structured_output.thesis: This is a copycat on a one-tweet Pokémon story, from a serial deployer who has already exited. The flow looks bundled, supply is heavily concentrated, and the price just collapsed 63%. The most likely paths are a slow bleed through the -50% stop or a liquidity pull, not a 2x.
